challenge.better_approach: In-house: troubles are files (3.4.3); Rescue is the recovery device (6.5). Grepped tickets: none builds the shell fallover.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That every uncommitted crossing came through a verb (sail cross/verdict) rather than a close that failed midway: measured only for the three FIXME and one SUPERSEDED crossings I know; the 7cae18f7f9c2 BUILDME crossing's path is unread.
challenge.prior_art: Looked: letting the Python launcher file its own trouble (set aside: outline 2.3.7.1.3 wants trouble to report when nothing else can, so Python may be the thing that is down).
challenge.real_collision: Possible with 12443bcc113f (another ticket's records do not refuse a crossing): committing own records at the verb is consistent with it; no Law contradicted. Distinction recorded.

answers.falsifier: with no Python reachable, cairn.cmd writes a trouble file in the trouble format and a repeat increments the matching open one
answers.from_idea: none, because it is a measured gap: see cairn/devices/recovery/intention+why.json
answers.how: A hypothesis, not a settled shape: the Python launcher exits with one reserved code (outline 5.4.3.8.3) only for its own failure; the shell shim (cairn.cmd first, then bin/cairn's floor on Linux) maps that code, and any failure to start Python, to a trouble file in the trouble format (finding a matching open one and incrementing it) and then to Rescue's entry. Depends on 380d524e6e9c.
answers.traces_to: Law 7 (permanent in records of truth: a crossing that exists on one disk is not permanent); Law 4 (enforced by physics, not by a hand remembering sail step 10); Law 5 (the repo is itself the state of the machine).
answers.what: The platform shell in front of the launcher falls over to Rescue on a launcher failure, writing the trouble file itself when Python cannot run (outline 5.4.3.8.1-3).

bullets.text: Measured: 2026-11-20 read of bin/cairn.cmd on akiendell: five lines, it runs bash by a hardcoded path and returns its exit code; it has no fallover, no trouble file and no reserved exit code. bin/cairn on Linux has _floor_refuse (a refusal with one remedy) but files no trouble ticket and does not call Rescue. Outline 5.4.3.8.1-3 says it must. No ticket builds it (open-198248431b60 answered by measurement, 2026-11-19).

title: The platform shell in front of the launcher falls over to Rescue on a launcher failure, writing the trouble file itself
